type: official primary laboratory survey experiment and procedure
publisher: Michael F. Schober, Frederick G. Conrad, Scott S. Fricker / BLS research paper
version: 1999; seven PDF pages; comparison groups reuse Schober/Conrad1997 study
observed: 33 Census interviewers/66 paid respondents in three new training groups; factual public-survey questions answered from fictional scenarios with defined correct answers. Straightforward mappings were accurate across strategies. Complicated mappings benefited from clarification and interviews took longer. Training separated scripted/paraphrased and requested/unsolicited definitions.
limitations: The circumstances are fictional but measured interviews are real; supplied dialogue examples are training illustrations, not observed transcript pairs. Two extreme conditions are reused earlier-study groups, not five newly randomized groups. Aggregate interview-minute/accuracy association is not an individual causal slope and cannot price GitHub wait time. The paper has an internal 10/26=42% arithmetic mismatch; do not reuse that percentage.
